corpusOverrides.note: 珈 started on the Japanese file, which writes the 王 vertical before its second bar (2·3 at 103°·91°). Make Me a Hanzi carries the dictionary order with no stroke over 22°, so the corpus was replaced instead of the stroke order. selection.json records the starting corpus and the reason.

directionProbe.threshold: angle over 60° between dictionary and candidate start-to-end vectors
directionProbe.note: Fourteen flagged characters were resolved by reordering (桷, 蕑, 减, 橿, 秬, 黥, 楛, 觚, 觳), by an authored path (蠲, 煢, 槀, 稾) or by both (雞); 珈 was resolved by changing corpus. The endpoint assignment check added 繳, whose 糸 strokes run in the same direction and differ only in order. Recomputed against the published order and paths, no stroke is over 60°.

subThresholdSlants.method: direction-probe rows recomputed against the published order and paths: 5 rows between 45° and 60°, none corrected
subThresholdSlants.note: Four are short dots the dictionary draws vertically while the licensed corpora slant them (袪 1 at 50°, 褰 1 and 11 at 59°, 鶊 1 at 51°), and one is the short 灬 dot of 黥 13 at 45°. Kept as licensed geometry, as in the earlier batches.

sourceTransform.note: serve.py, source-checks.mjs and direction-probe.mjs accept translate(x, -y); no glyph in this batch carries a horizontal offset.
